epithet.ko: 1794년 방데를 휩쓴 지옥 종대를 조직한 서부군 총사령관
epithet.en: Commander of the Army of the West who organised the infernal columns that swept the Vendée in 1794

bio.ko: 1756년 에브뢰에서 태어나 1789년부터 혁명을 지지해 아비롱 시장을 지내고 국유재산을 사들였다. 1792년 외르 의용대대 장교로 북부 전선에 나갔고, 1793년 방데에서 두 달 싸운 뒤 동피레네군을 지휘했다. 1793년 12월 30일 서부군 총사령관이 되어 1794년 1월 열두 개 종대에 반란에 가담한 「도적」을 여자와 아이까지 죽이고 마을을 불태우라고 지시했다. 지옥 종대는 넉 달 동안 민간인 2만~5만 명을 죽였으나 봉기를 되살렸고, 그는 5월 해임되고 9월 체포되었다. 1795년 12월 군사재판은 명령을 따랐을 뿐이라며 무죄를 선고했고, 그는 1803~1811년 주미 대사와 1812년 제국 남작으로 출세한 뒤 1816년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Évreux in 1756, he backed the Revolution from 1789, served as mayor of Aviron and bought confiscated church property. An officer of the Eure volunteers on the northern frontier in 1792, he fought two months in the Vendée in 1793 and then commanded the Army of the Eastern Pyrenees. Taking command of the Army of the West on 30 December 1793, in January 1794 he ordered twelve columns to bayonet the “brigands” who had joined the revolt, women and children included, and to burn the villages. In four months these infernal columns killed 20,000 to 50,000 civilians but revived the rising; he was recalled in May 1794 and arrested in September. A military tribunal acquitted him in December 1795 because he had only obeyed orders, and he prospered as ambassador to the United States from 1803 to 1811 and a baron of the Empire in 1812, dying unprosecuted in 1816.

evidence.excerpt: 4 July 1756 – 10 December 1816

evidence.claim: French Army officer and diplomat
evidence.excerpt: was a French Army officer and diplomat who served in the French Revolutionary Wars

evidence.claim: born in Évreux, Normandy
evidence.excerpt: né le 4 juillet 1756 à Évreux et mort le 10 décembre 1816 à Conches-en-Ouche

evidence.claim: fervent revolutionary, mayor of Aviron, bought church property
evidence.excerpt: Turreau was nevertheless a fervent revolutionary from 1789, profiting like many others, especially the bourgeois of that era. Elected mayor of Aviron, he bought several clerical estates

evidence.claim: captain of Eure volunteers, northern frontier, colonel
evidence.excerpt: In September he was elected captain of a company of volunteers from Eure and set out to fight on the northern frontiers. Made a colonel in November, he was integrated into the Army of the Moselle.

evidence.claim: two months in the Vendée; Army of the Eastern Pyrenees
evidence.excerpt: Even so, he fought for two months in the Vendée. He served as head of the Army of the Eastern Pyrenees from 12 October until 27 November 1793.

evidence.claim: commander in chief of the Army of the West from 29 December
evidence.excerpt: He became commander in chief of the Armée de l'Ouest from 29 December, but he again regarded this post with little enthusiasm.

evidence.claim: instructions of 19 January 1794
evidence.excerpt: La consigne est de passer au fil de la baïonnette tous les rebelles « trouvés les armes à la main, ou convaincus de les avoir prises », ainsi que « les filles, femmes et enfants qui seront dans ce cas ».

evidence.claim: 20,000 to 50,000 civilians killed in four months; the war revived
evidence.excerpt: Entre 20 000 et 50 000 civils périssent en quatre mois à cause de ces massacres.

evidence.claim: recalled 18 May 1794, arrested 28 September, a year in prison, memoirs
evidence.locator: Suite de la carrière de Turreau
evidence.excerpt: Louis Marie Turreau est rappelé dès le 18 mai 1794. [...] Mais il est arrêté le 28 septembre de la même année. Il passe une année en prison et en profite pour rédiger ses Mémoires pour servir à l’histoire de la Vendée.

evidence.claim: acquitted 19 December 1795 for having obeyed orders
evidence.excerpt: On 19 December 1795 he was acquitted by a military tribunal which judged he had only been obeying orders.

evidence.claim: envoy to Switzerland, ambassador to the USA 1803–1811
evidence.excerpt: Under the French Consulate he was sent as an envoy to Switzerland. [...] From 1803 to 1811 he was French ambassador to the United States of America

evidence.claim: baron of the Empire 1812
evidence.excerpt: Louis Marie Turreau est créé baron de l'Empire le 13 mars 1812.

evidence.claim: submitted to Louis XVIII, not prosecuted
evidence.excerpt: In 1814, he submitted to Louis XVIII [...] On the Bourbon Restoration he was not prosecuted, either for libel or for the infernal columns.

evidence.claim: General of the Republic; commander in chief of the Army of the West, December 1793 – May 1794
evidence.excerpt: He became commander in chief of the Armée de l'Ouest from 29 December

evidence.claim: French ambassador to the United States under the Consulate and Empire
evidence.excerpt: From 1803 to 1811 he was French ambassador to the United States of America

epithet.en: Representative on mission of the Convention who ordered the drownings at Nantes

bio.ko: 1756년 오리야크 근처 욜레의 소작농 집안에서 태어나 소송대리인이 되었고, 혁명이 일어나자 국민방위대와 자코뱅 클럽에 들어갔다. 1792년 캉탈 선출 국민공회 의원으로 코르들리에와 자코뱅의 연설가였고 루이 16세 처형에 찬성했으며 지롱드파 축출에 가담했다. 1793년 가을 낭트에 파견되어 갈레른 행군에서 잡힌 포로가 쌓이자 12월부터 1794년 2월까지 바닥에 구멍을 낸 배로 루아르강에 가라앉히는 익사형과 집단 총살로 감옥을 비웠다. 그가 「수직 유배」라 부른 익사형으로 1,800~4,800명, 총살로 2,600명이 죽었다. 1794년 2월 소환된 뒤 튀로의 방침을 옹호했고 테르미도르에 가담했으나 낭트 혁명위원회 재판에서 기소되어 12월 16일 단두대에 올랐다.
bio.en: Born in 1756 at Yolet near Aurillac into a tenant-farming family, he became a procurator and, when the Revolution came, joined the National Guard and the Jacobin Club. Elected to the Convention for Cantal in 1792, an orator of the Cordeliers and Jacobins, he voted for the execution of Louis XVI and took part in the fall of the Girondins. Sent to Nantes in the autumn of 1793, where prisoners from the Virée de Galerne were piling up, from December 1793 to February 1794 he emptied the prisons by mass shootings and by drownings in the Loire on barges with trap-door bottoms. The drownings, which he called “vertical deportation”, killed 1,800 to 4,800 people and the shootings 2,600. Recalled in February 1794, he defended Turreau’s methods and joined the overthrow of Robespierre, but the trial of the Nantes revolutionary committee turned on him and he was guillotined on 16 December 1794.

evidence.excerpt: 16 March 1756 – 16 December 1794

evidence.claim: French revolutionary politician, deputy to the National Convention
evidence.excerpt: was a French Revolutionary, politician and convicted war criminal most notable for his actions in the War in the Vendée during the Reign of Terror

evidence.claim: born at Yolet near Aurillac in Auvergne
evidence.excerpt: Carrier was born at Yolet, a village near Aurillac in upper Auvergne, as the fourth of six children born to Jean Carrier and Marguerite Puex.

evidence.claim: tenant-farmer family; law office; National Guard and Jacobin Club
evidence.excerpt: As the son of a middle class tenant farmer, Carrier and his family survived on income reaped from cultivating the land of a French nobleman. [...] with the outbreak of the Revolution joined the National Guard and the Jacobin Club.

evidence.claim: procurator at Aurillac 1784
evidence.excerpt: En 1784, Jean-Baptiste Carrier, à force de travail, parvient à obtenir la place de procureur à Aurillac, mais son office est supprimé en 1789.

evidence.claim: deputy for Cantal; Cordeliers and Jacobins
evidence.excerpt: in 1792 was elected deputy to the National Convention for Cantal. He was already known as one of the influential members of the Cordeliers and the Jacobin Club.

evidence.claim: voted for the king's death; fall of the Girondins
evidence.excerpt: He voted in favor of the execution of deposed King Louis XVI, was one of the first to call for the arrest of the Duke of Orléans and took a prominent part in the overthrow of the Girondists (on 31 May).

evidence.claim: missions in Normandy and Rennes, then Nantes
evidence.excerpt: Après ses missions en Normandie et une autre à Rennes, il est envoyé à Nantes en vendémiaire an II (septembre 1793) pour faire cesser la révolte vendéenne par les moyens les plus extrêmes.

evidence.claim: drownings in barges with trap doors
evidence.excerpt: In the following days Carrier put large numbers of prisoners aboard vessels with trap doors for bottoms, and sank them in the Loire river. These executions included priests and nuns, as well as women and children. They were known as the Drownings at Nantes.

evidence.claim: 2,600 shot
evidence.excerpt: De la fin décembre 1793 à la fin février 1794, 2 600 prisonniers sont fusillés.

evidence.claim: "vertical deportation"
evidence.excerpt: procédé que Carrier appelait « la déportation verticale », la Loire étant en conséquence qualifiée dans ses écrits de « fleuve républicain »

evidence.claim: recalled 8 February 1794; defended Turreau
evidence.excerpt: Carrier demande dans le même temps son rappel à Paris, qu'il obtient le 8 février 1794. [...] Après son rappel, Carrier prend publiquement position en faveur du général Turreau

evidence.claim: joined Thermidor; arrested 3 September 1794
evidence.excerpt: Il prend part à la chute de Robespierre le 9 thermidor an II (27 juillet 1794). [...] ils décrètent son arrestation le 3 septembre 1794.

evidence.claim: guillotined 16 December 1794
evidence.excerpt: Along with two accomplices from the revolutionary committee of Nantes, Carrier was executed by the guillotine in Paris, on 16 December 1794.

evidence.claim: Deputy for Cantal in the National Convention; representative on mission at Nantes
evidence.excerpt: in 1792 was elected deputy to the National Convention for Cantal

evidence.claim: Member of the Jacobin Club
evidence.excerpt: with the outbreak of the Revolution joined the National Guard and the Jacobin Club

evidence.claim: Influential member of the Cordeliers
evidence.excerpt: He was already known as one of the influential members of the Cordeliers and the Jacobin Club.

r.en: Procurator at Aurillac
Deputy for Cantal in the National Convention
Representative on mission at Nantes; directed the drownings and shootings
Arrested, condemned by the Revolutionary Tribunal and guillotined

epithet.ko: 마인츠군을 이끌고 르망과 사부네에서 방데군을 깨뜨린 공화국 장군
epithet.en: Republican general who led the Army of Mainz and broke the Vendéan army at Le Mans and Savenay

bio.ko: 1753년 스트라스부르의 석공 집안에서 태어나 건축을 공부했고, 신성 로마 제국군 장교로 7년을 복무하다 평민 출신이라 승진이 막히자 돌아와 벨포르의 공공건물 감독관이 되었다. 1792년 오랭 의용대대에 들어가 1793년 마인츠 방어로 이름을 얻었고, 여단장으로 마인츠군과 함께 방데에 파견되었다. 토르푸에서 패했으나 10월 숄레의 승리에 기여해 사단장이 되었고, 마르소와 함께 12월 르망과 사부네에서 가톨릭 왕당군을 섬멸했다. 1794년 1월 튀로에게 주민의 신뢰를 얻고 반군 집결지만 치자는 안을 냈다가 거부당했고, 방데인에게 관대해야 한다고 말해 소환되었다. 뒤에 플뢰뤼스와 라인 전선에서 싸웠고 이집트 원정군을 지휘하다 1800년 카이로에서 암살되었다.
bio.en: Born in 1753 in Strasbourg, the son of a master builder, he studied architecture, served seven years as an officer of the Holy Roman Emperor and returned as inspector of public buildings at Belfort. He enlisted in the Haut-Rhin volunteers in 1792, won renown in the defence of Mainz in 1793 and was sent as a brigade general with the Army of Mainz to the Vendée. Beaten at Torfou, he contributed to the victory at Cholet in October, was promoted divisional general and, with Marceau, destroyed the Catholic and Royal Army at Le Mans and Savenay in December. In January 1794 Turreau rejected his plan to win the inhabitants’ trust and attack only rebel gatherings, and his opinion that the Vendéans deserved lenient measures got him recalled. He later fought at Fleurus and on the Rhine, commanded the army in Egypt and was assassinated in Cairo on 14 June 1800.

evidence.excerpt: 9 March 1753 – 14 June 1800

evidence.claim: French army officer
evidence.excerpt: was a French army officer and architect who served in the War of the Bavarian Succession and French Revolutionary Wars

evidence.claim: born in Strasbourg, Alsace
evidence.excerpt: Jean-Baptiste Kléber was born on 9 March 1753 in Strasbourg, in the province of Alsace, where his father worked as a master builder.

evidence.claim: studied architecture; Austrian service; left 1783
evidence.excerpt: Finding that his humble birth hindered his chances for promotion beyond that of an unterleutnant, he left the Austrian army in 1783 after serving seven years.

evidence.claim: inspector of public buildings at Belfort
evidence.excerpt: On returning to France, Kléber received the appointment of inspector of public buildings at Belfort.

evidence.claim: Haut-Rhin volunteers 1792; Mainz 1793; brigade general
evidence.excerpt: In 1792, at the start of the French Revolutionary Wars, Kléber enlisted in the 4th Battalion of Volunteers of Haut-Rhin. [...] At the defense of Mainz in July 1793 he so distinguished himself that [...] was promoted to brigade general in August 1793.

evidence.claim: Tiffauges defeat; Cholet; divisional general
evidence.excerpt: Although beaten at the Battle of Tiffauges on 19 September 1793, he maintained good relations with the representatives on mission and managed to keep his command. A month later, Kléber contributed to the Republican victory at Cholet, earning him his promotion to divisional general on 17 October 1793.

evidence.claim: Le Mans and Savenay with Marceau
evidence.excerpt: In these operations began his intimacy with General François Marceau, with whom he defeated the Royalists at the battles of Le Mans and Savenay in December 1793.

evidence.claim: plan of 7 January 1794 rejected by Turreau
evidence.excerpt: Le 7 janvier 1794, Kléber soumet un plan au général Turreau. [...] Il propose de protéger les côtes des Anglais, d'encercler et de quadriller le territoire insurgé en utilisant des camps fortifiés comme points d'appui, de gagner la confiance des habitants et enfin de n'attaquer que les rassemblements des rebelles. Mais ce plan est rejeté par Turreau

evidence.claim: recalled for advocating lenient measures
evidence.excerpt: When Kléber openly expressed his opinion that the Vendéans merited lenient measures, the authorities recalled him, but reinstated him once more in April 1794 and sent him to the Army of the Ardennes.

evidence.claim: Fleurus; Rhine; Egypt; Heliopolis
evidence.excerpt: Although he had only 10,000 men against 60,000 Turks, Kléber's forces utterly defeated the Ottomans on 20 March 1800.

evidence.claim: assassinated in Cairo 14 June 1800
evidence.excerpt: The assassination happened in Cairo on 14 June 1800, coincidentally the same day on which Kléber's friend and comrade, Desaix, fell at Marengo.

evidence.claim: General of the Republic: Mainz, the Vendée, Fleurus, the Rhine, Egypt
evidence.excerpt: Kléber was then posted to the Army of the Coasts of La Rochelle and deployed to Western France, where he took part in the suppression of the Revolt in the Vendée.

r.en: Officer in the army of the Holy Roman Emperor
Inspector of public buildings at Belfort
Defence of Mainz; brigade general
Led the Army of Mainz in the Vendée: Cholet, Le Mans, Savenay
Army of Sambre and Meuse; Fleurus and the Rhine
Commander in chief of the French army in Egypt

epithet.ko: 키브롱에서 망명군을 무찌르고 1796년 방데를 평정한 공화국 장군
epithet.en: Republican general who crushed the émigré landing at Quiberon and pacified the Vendée in 1796

bio.ko: 1768년 베르사유 근교에서 왕실 사냥터 마부의 아들로 태어나 1784년 근위연대 사병으로 입대했다. 1792년 장교가 되어 됭케르크 방어로 1793년 사단장과 모젤군 사령관에 올랐고 12월 알자스에서 오스트리아군을 몰아냈다. 1794년 3월 피슈그뤼의 고발로 체포되어 테르미도르 뒤에야 풀려났다. 서부의 연안군 사령관으로 1795년 2월 라자주네 조약으로 이어진 화해를 마무리했고, 7월 키브롱에서 영국이 실어 온 망명군을 섬멸했다. 12월 서부 전군을 지휘하게 되어 기동 종대와 사면, 예배의 자유로 1796년 스토플레와 샤레트를 잡아 방데 전쟁을 끝내고 슈앙의 항복을 받았다. 아일랜드 원정에 실패했고 1797년 잠시 전쟁장관을 지낸 뒤 29세로 병사했다.
bio.en: Born in 1768 near Versailles, a groom’s son, he enlisted as a private in the French Guards in 1784. Commissioned in 1792, he rose to divisional general and command of the Army of the Moselle in 1793 and drove the Austrians from Alsace. Arrested in March 1794 after a denunciation by Pichegru, he was freed only after Thermidor. Commanding the coastal armies in the west, he completed the conciliation that led to the Treaty of La Jaunaye in February 1795 and annihilated the émigré force landed by the British at Quiberon in July. Supreme commander in the west from December, he used disciplined mobile columns, amnesty and freedom of worship to capture Stofflet and Charette in 1796, ending the War in the Vendée, and took the surrender of the Chouans. His Irish expedition failed; he was briefly Minister of War in 1797 and died of tuberculosis aged 29.

evidence.excerpt: 24 June 1768 – 19 September 1797

evidence.claim: French Army officer and Minister of War
evidence.excerpt: was a French Army officer and politician who served as the Minister of War in 1797

evidence.claim: born at Montreuil, Versailles
evidence.excerpt: Lazare Hoche was born on 24 June 1768 in the village of Montreuil, today part of Versailles, to Anne Merlière and Louis Hoche, a groom at the royal hunting grounds.

evidence.claim: French Guards 1784; National Guard 1789
evidence.excerpt: He enlisted in the French Guards Regiment as a fusilier in October 1784 [...] Hoche joined the new National Guard in September 1789.

evidence.claim: Dunkirk; general of division October 1793; Army of the Moselle
evidence.excerpt: he took part in the successful defence of Dunkirk, for which he was promoted successively to colonel and brigade general in September, and to general of division in October 1793. In November, Hoche was provisionally appointed to command the Army of the Moselle

evidence.claim: drove Wurmser from Alsace
evidence.excerpt: In the Second Battle of Wissembourg on 26 December 1793, the French under his command drove Dagobert Sigmund von Wurmser's Austrian army from Alsace.

evidence.claim: arrested 1794, freed after Thermidor
evidence.excerpt: he was arrested on orders of the Committee of Public Safety, charges of treason having been proffered by Charles Pichegru [...] and was only released on 4 August, after the fall of Maximilien Robespierre and the end of the Reign of Terror.

evidence.claim: Army of the Coasts of Cherbourg and Brest; La Jaunaye
evidence.locator: War in the Vendée and Chouannerie
evidence.excerpt: Hoche completed the work of his predecessors in a few months by the Treaty of La Jaunaye (15 February 1795), but soon afterwards the war was renewed by the rebel leadership.

evidence.claim: Quiberon 21 July 1795
evidence.locator: War in the Vendée and Chouannerie
evidence.excerpt: He decisively defeated the Royalist invaders at Fort Penthièvre on 21 July.

evidence.claim: supreme commander in the west December 1795
evidence.locator: War in the Vendée and Chouannerie
evidence.excerpt: In December 1795, when the three armies previously under his command [...] merged to form the new Army of the Coasts of the Ocean, Hoche became the supreme commander of all Republican forces in Western France.

evidence.claim: Stofflet and Charette captured; Chouans surrender
evidence.locator: War in the Vendée and Chouannerie
evidence.excerpt: Hoche directed the operations that led to the capture (and subsequent execution) of rebel leaders Jean-Nicolas Stofflet (24 February 1796) and François de Charette (23 March), bringing an end to the War in the Vendée. With the surrender of the leaders of the Chouannerie, in May and June 1796, Hoche concluded the pacification of Western France

evidence.claim: Irish expedition
evidence.excerpt: The fleet set sail for Ireland on 15 December 1796, with Hoche and Morard de Galles aboard the frigate Fraternité.

evidence.claim: Minister of War July 1797
evidence.excerpt: In July 1797, Hoche was appointed the Minister of War by the Directory.

evidence.claim: died at Wetzlar of tuberculosis aged 29
evidence.excerpt: he died at Wetzlar on 19 September of consumption (tuberculosis), aged 29

evidence.locator: War in the Vendée and Chouannerie
evidence.claim: General of the Republic; supreme commander of the Republican forces in western France, 1795–1796
evidence.excerpt: Hoche became the supreme commander of all Republican forces in Western France

evidence.claim: Minister of War under the Directory, July 1797
evidence.excerpt: In July 1797, Hoche was appointed the Minister of War by the Directory.

r.en: Private in the French Guards
Commander of the Army of the Moselle; recovered Alsace

r.en: Arrested on the Committee of Public Safety's orders; freed after Thermidor
Commander of the Armies of the Coasts of Cherbourg and Brest; victory at Quiberon
Commander in chief of the Army of the Coasts of the Ocean; pacification of the Vendée
Commander of the Army of Sambre and Meuse; Minister of War

epithet.ko: 「방데의 도살자」로 불린 공화국 여단장, 당통파와 함께 처형
epithet.en: Republican brigade general called “the butcher of the Vendée”, executed with the Dantonists

bio.ko: 1751년 알자스 몰스하임에서 태어나 경기병으로 복무한 뒤 1790년 아그노 시 서기가 되었다. 1792년 파리에서 당통과 가까워졌고 8월 10일 튈르리궁 습격에서 연맹병 부대를 이끌었다. 뒤무리에의 참모로 종군하다 1793년 4월 그의 배반 뒤 체포되었으나 무죄를 입증하고 여단장이 되어 방데로 보내졌다. 라로셸 연안군 전위로 6월 파르트네와 7월 샤티용을 점령했으나 7월 5일 샤티용에서 대패해 정직되었다가 복직했다. 갈레른 행군 때 패배를 거듭했으나 르망과 사부네에서 왕당군 섬멸에 가담했고, 사부네 뒤 포로 500~700명을 총살했다. 「방데는 더 이상 없다」는 편지는 진위가 다투어진다. 1794년 당통의 벗으로 기소되어 4월 5일 당통파와 함께 처형되었다.
bio.en: Born in 1751 at Molsheim in Alsace, he served in a hussar regiment and in 1790 became clerk of Haguenau. In Paris from 1792 he became an ally of Danton and commanded fédérés in the attack on the Tuileries on 10 August. On Dumouriez’s staff, he was arrested after the general’s defection in April 1793, cleared and sent to the Vendée as a brigade general. Leading the vanguard of the Army of the Coasts of La Rochelle, he took Parthenay in June and Châtillon on 3 July, but was routed at Châtillon on 5 July and suspended. Beaten repeatedly in the Virée de Galerne, he took part in the destruction of the Catholic and Royal Army at Le Mans and Savenay, after which his hussars shot 500 to 700 prisoners. The letter attributed to him beginning “There is no more Vendée” is of disputed authenticity. Proscribed as a friend of Danton, he was guillotined with the Dantonists on 5 April 1794.

evidence.excerpt: 5 September 1751 – 5 April 1794

evidence.claim: French Army officer, brigade general
evidence.excerpt: was a French Army officer. He is best known as one of the main French Republican commanders in the initial stage of the War in the Vendée.

evidence.claim: born at Molsheim, Alsace
evidence.excerpt: Westermann was born on 5 September 1751 in Molsheim, Alsace (today department of Bas-Rhin).

evidence.claim: hussars 1767; clerk of Haguenau 1790
evidence.excerpt: He enlisted in Count Esterhazy's regiment of hussars in 1767, retiring six years later as a non-commissioned officer. [...] in 1790 became greffier of the municipality of Haguenau.

evidence.claim: ally of Danton; 10 August 1792
evidence.excerpt: Westermann moved to Paris in May 1792, where he became an ally of revolutionary leader Georges Danton. Westermann played a leading role in the insurrection of 10 August 1792, where he commanded a unit of fédérés in the attack on the Tuileries Palace.

evidence.claim: with Dumouriez; arrested; cleared; brigade general
evidence.excerpt: but was arrested as an accomplice after the general's defection in April 1793. Denounced by Jean-Paul Marat to the National Convention, Westermann succeeded in proving his innocence, and was promoted to brigade general and sent to quell the Revolt in the Vendée.

evidence.claim: vanguard; Parthenay; Châtillon; suspended; restored 29 August
evidence.excerpt: Appointed commander of the vanguard of the Army of the Coasts of La Rochelle on 18 May 1793, he defeated the rebels at Parthenay on 20 June, then captured Châtillon on 3 July. After suffering a defeat at the First Battle of Châtillon, Westermann was suspended and brought before the National Convention, only recovering his command on 29 August.

evidence.claim: Croix-Bataille, Entrammes, Le Mans, Savenay
evidence.excerpt: Beaten at the battles of Croix-Bataille and Entrames, he defeated the Vendéens at Beaupréau, Granville, and in December 1793 annihilated the Catholic and Royal Army at the Battle of Le Mans and the Battle of Savenay.

evidence.claim: shot 500 to 700 prisoners near Prinquiau
evidence.excerpt: Westermann and his hussards shot 500 to 700 prisoners, men, women, and children, at the Sem forest near Prinquiau.

evidence.claim: the disputed letter
evidence.excerpt: In a controversial document, the authenticity of which is disputed, Westermann supposedly wrote to the Committee of Public Safety: "There is no more Vendée, Republican citizens.

evidence.claim: "le boucher de la Vendée"
evidence.excerpt: portent le nom de celui qui fut surnommé « le boucher de la Vendée »

evidence.claim: guillotined with the Dantonists 5 April 1794
evidence.excerpt: After his victory, in January 1794 Westermann was summoned to Paris, where, as a friend and partisan of Danton, he was proscribed and sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Tribunal. He was guillotined along with the Dantonist party on 5 April 1794.

evidence.claim: Brigade general; commander of the vanguard of the Army of the Coasts of La Rochelle, then in the Army of the West
evidence.excerpt: Appointed commander of the vanguard of the Army of the Coasts of La Rochelle on 18 May 1793

evidence.claim: Commanded fédérés in the insurrection of 10 August 1792
evidence.excerpt: Westermann played a leading role in the insurrection of 10 August 1792, where he commanded a unit of fédérés in the attack on the Tuileries Palace.

r.en: Clerk of the municipality of Haguenau
Commanded fédérés on 10 August 1792
On Dumouriez's staff with the Army of the North
Brigade general; commander of the vanguard of the Army of the Coasts of La Rochelle
Army of the West; Le Mans and Savenay
Executed with the Dantonists

epithet.ko: 카틀리노의 뒤를 이은 가톨릭 왕당군 제2대 총사령관, 누아르무티에에서 총살
epithet.en: Second generalissimo of the Catholic and Royal Army after Cathelineau, shot at Noirmoutier

bio.ko: 1752년 드레스덴에서 폴란드 왕의 고문이던 프랑스인 아버지에게서 태어나 1757년 프랑스에 귀화했다. 왕실 기병 장교로 복무하다 1783년 제대해 앙주의 보프레오에 은거했고, 1790년 연맹제에 멘에루아르 대표로 참석할 만큼 혁명에 호의적이었다. 1793년 3월 징집에 맞서 봉기한 농민들이 군 경험을 보고 그를 지휘관으로 끌어냈다. 4월 슈미예에서 포로 학살을 요구하는 부하들에게 주기도문을 외우게 하고 「하느님께 거짓말하지 말라」며 포로를 살렸다. 카틀리노가 죽자 7월 19일 총사령관으로 뽑혔으나 뤼송에서 두 번 패했고, 10월 숄레에서 중상을 입어 누아르무티에섬으로 옮겨졌다. 1794년 1월 3일 섬을 점령한 공화국군에 붙잡혀 안락의자에 앉은 채 총살되었다.
bio.en: Born in 1752 in Dresden to a French father who was a privy councillor of the King of Poland, he was naturalised French in 1757. An officer of royal cavalry, he resigned in 1783 and retired to Beaupréau in Anjou, and represented Maine-et-Loire at the Fête de la Fédération in 1790. In March 1793 the peasants who had risen against conscription forced him to lead them because of his military experience. At Chemillé in April he saved the Republican prisoners his men wanted to kill by making them recite the Lord’s Prayer and breaking in with “Do not lie to God”. Elected generalissimo on 19 July 1793 after Cathelineau’s death, he was twice beaten at Luçon and gravely wounded at Cholet in October, and was carried to the island of Noirmoutier. Captured when Republican troops took the island on 3 January 1794, unable to stand, he was shot in an armchair. His wife was shot on 29 January.

evidence.excerpt: né le 21 mars 1752 à Dresde et mort entre le 6 et le 9 janvier 1794 à Noirmoutier, est un militaire français

evidence.claim: French soldier, naturalised in 1757
evidence.excerpt: Il est naturalisé français en 1757.

evidence.claim: French family established at Dresden
evidence.excerpt: Maurice d'Elbee was born in Dresden, Electorate of Saxony to a French family in 1752.

evidence.claim: father privy councillor of the King of Poland at Dresden
evidence.excerpt: Fils de Maurice Gigost d'Elbée, seigneur de la Gobinière et de La Loge-Vaugirault (1695-1763), alors conseiller privé du Roi de Pologne établi à Dresde, en Saxe

evidence.claim: royal cavalry 1772–1783; retired to Beaupréau
evidence.excerpt: Le 1er juin 1772, il est sous-lieutenant au régiment du Dauphin cavalerie et le 6 mai 1781, il est lieutenant au 5e régiment de chevau-légers. Il démissionne de l'armée le 17 septembre 1783. Il se retire alors à Beaupréau, en Anjou.

evidence.claim: favourable to the Revolution; Fête de la Fédération 1790
evidence.excerpt: En 1789, d'Elbée se montre d'abord favorable à la Révolution française. Le 14 juillet 1790, il participe à la Fête de la Fédération à Paris, où il représente le Maine-et-Loire.

evidence.claim: forced to lead the insurgents in March 1793
evidence.locator: Général de l'Armée catholique et royale
evidence.excerpt: Les paysans insurgés viennent trouver d'Elbée en raison de son expérience militaire et le contraignent à prendre la tête de leur rassemblement.

evidence.claim: the "Pater de d'Elbée" at Chemillé
evidence.locator: Général de l'Armée catholique et royale
evidence.excerpt: d'Elbée les interrompt : « Arrêtez ! Ne mentez pas à Dieu ! [...] ». Ces déclarations ne provoquent aucune contestation et les prisonniers sont ainsi sauvés. L'épisode est alors appelé le « Pater de d'Elbée ».

evidence.claim: elected generalissimo 19 July 1793; defeats at Luçon
evidence.locator: Général de l'Armée catholique et royale
evidence.excerpt: Le 19 juillet, d'Elbée est élu par un conseil de guerre généralissime de Armée catholique et royale pour succéder à Jacques Cathelineau. Il décide d'attaquer la ville de Luçon mais il subit deux lourdes défaites devant cette ville le 30 juillet et le 14 août.

evidence.claim: wounded at Cholet; carried to Noirmoutier
evidence.excerpt: Le 17 octobre 1793, l'armée vendéenne est complètement défaite à la bataille de Cholet et d'Elbée est grièvement blessé lors des combats. Il ne prend pas part à la virée de Galerne

evidence.claim: captured 3 January 1794, shot in an armchair
evidence.excerpt: Le 3 janvier 1794, les troupes républicaines débarquent sur l'île de Noirmoutier et la garnison vendéenne capitule. D'Elbée est rapidement découvert et fait prisonnier. [...] D'Elbée est exécuté entre le 6 et le 9 janvier. Incapable de marcher, il est porté sur un fauteuil jusqu'à la place d'Armes.

evidence.claim: wife shot 29 January 1794
evidence.excerpt: L'épouse de d'Elbée, Marguerite-Charlotte Duhoux d'Hauterive, est quant à elle fusillée le 29 janvier

evidence.claim: General, then generalissimo of the Catholic and Royal Army, July–October 1793
evidence.excerpt: Chef royaliste pendant la guerre de Vendée, il est généralissime de l'Armée catholique et royale, succédant à Cathelineau, de juillet à octobre 1793.

evidence.claim: Officer of royal cavalry
evidence.excerpt: Le 1er juin 1772, il est sous-lieutenant au régiment du Dauphin cavalerie et le 6 mai 1781, il est lieutenant au 5e régiment de chevau-légers.

r.en: Officer of royal cavalry
Maine-et-Loire representative at the Fête de la Fédération
Commander of the Vendéan insurgents: Chemillé, Thouars, Fontenay
Generalissimo of the Catholic and Royal Army
Captured at Noirmoutier and shot

epithet.ko: 사냥터지기에서 앙주군 사령관이 된 방데의 장군, 앙제에서 총살
epithet.en: Gamekeeper who became commander of the Vendéan army of Anjou, shot at Angers

bio.ko: 1753년 로렌의 바텔레몽에서 방앗간 주인의 아들로 태어나 오랫동안 스위스 연대 사병으로 복무했고, 뒤에 몰레브리에에서 백작의 사냥터지기가 되었다. 1793년 3월 앙주의 봉기 때 옛 군인으로서 지휘관에 추대되어 카틀리노와 함께 생플로랑르비에이를 점령했고, 델베 휘하에서 퐁트네·숄레·라발·앙트랭 전투에 참여했다. 왕당군 소장이 되었고 1794년 1월 라로슈자클랭이 전사하자 사령관이 되어 지옥 종대를 피해 모여든 농민들과 2월 8일 숄레를 잠시 되찾았다. 1795년 2월 라자주네에서 공화국 승인을 거부했으나 캉클로의 공세에 밀려 5월 2일 생플로랑르비에이에서 강화했다. 아르투아 백작의 명령으로 1796년 1월 다시 봉기했다가 2월 농가에서 붙잡혀 앙제에서 총살되었다.
bio.en: Born in 1753 at Bathelémont in Lorraine, a miller’s son, he served for long as a private in a Swiss regiment and later became a gamekeeper at Maulévrier. Chosen as a leader for his military past when Anjou rose in March 1793, he took Saint-Florent-le-Vieil with Cathelineau and fought under d’Elbée at Fontenay, Cholet, Laval and Antrain. Appointed major-general of the royalist army, he took command after La Rochejaquelein was killed in January 1794 and, with peasants fleeing the infernal columns, briefly retook Cholet on 8 February. At La Jaunaye in February 1795 he refused to recognise the Republic, but Canclaux’s offensive drove him to make peace on the same terms at Saint-Florent-le-Vieil on 2 May. On the orders of the Count of Artois he rose again in January 1796, was surprised in a farmhouse near La Poitevinière, condemned by a military commission at Angers and shot on 25 February.

evidence.excerpt: né le 3 février 1753 à Bathelémont (duché de Lorraine) et mort fusillé le 25 février 1796 à Angers, est un militaire français et un général royaliste de la guerre de Vendée

evidence.claim: French soldier and royalist general
evidence.excerpt: est un militaire français et un général royaliste de la guerre de Vendée

evidence.claim: born at Bathelémont, Lorraine, son of a miller
evidence.excerpt: Born in Bathelémont-lès-Bauzemont (Meurthe-et-Moselle), the son of a miller

evidence.claim: Swiss regiment; gamekeeper at Maulévrier
evidence.excerpt: Longtemps simple soldat dans un régiment suisse en France et ensuite garde-chasse au service du comte de Colbert-Maulévrier à Maulévrier, il rejoint les Vendéens quand ils se révoltent contre la Révolution

evidence.claim: chosen as leader in March 1793; Saint-Florent-le-Vieil
evidence.locator: Insurrection contre la levée en masse en mars 1793
evidence.excerpt: les insurgés prennent pour chefs d'anciens soldats comme Jean-Nicolas Stofflet et Jean Perdriau [...] Ils s'emparent de Saint-Florent-le-Vieil le 12 mars

evidence.claim: under d'Elbée; battles
evidence.excerpt: Pendant la guerre de Vendée, il sert d'abord sous le commandement de Maurice d'Elbée, se bat à Fontenay, Cholet et Beaupréau, Laval et Antrain.

evidence.claim: major-general; succeeded La Rochejaquelein in 1794
evidence.excerpt: Il est nommé major-général de l'armée royaliste et, en 1794, succède à Henri de La Rochejaquelein comme général en chef.

evidence.claim: retook Cholet 8 February 1794
evidence.excerpt: Le 8 février, désormais à la tête de 4 000 à 7 000 Vendéens, il attaque Cholet. Bien que défendue par 3 000 hommes, la ville est prise

evidence.claim: refused to recognise the Republic at La Jaunaye
evidence.locator: Les traités de La Jaunaye et de Saint-Florent-le-Vieil
evidence.excerpt: Les représentants lui offrent les mêmes conditions de paix qu'à Charette et Sapinaud, mais il refuse catégoriquement de reconnaître la République. Le 22 février, il rompt les négociations et regagne l'Anjou.

evidence.claim: peace at Saint-Florent-le-Vieil 2 May 1795
evidence.excerpt: le conduisent à faire sa soumission et à accepter les termes du traité de Saint-Florent-le-Vieil, le 2 mai 1795

evidence.claim: took up arms again for the comte de Provence; maréchal de camp
evidence.excerpt: Cependant, il viole bientôt ce traité et, en décembre 1795, reprend les armes à l'instigation d'agents royalistes pour le parti du comte de Provence, le futur Louis XVIII, de qui il a reçu le rang de maréchal de camp.

evidence.claim: rose on 26 January 1796 with 400 men on Artois's order
evidence.locator: Effondrement des armées vendéennes et victoire des républicains
evidence.excerpt: Stofflet, fait Lieutenant Général et chevalier de Saint-Louis, reste longtemps dans l'expectative avant de reprendre les armes sans illusion le 26 janvier sur ordre du comte d'Artois. Rejoint par seulement 400 hommes

evidence.claim: captured and shot at Angers 25 February 1796
evidence.excerpt: Il est surpris par un détachement républicain du régiment de Bassigny, la nuit du 23 au 24 février 1796 dans une métairie, la ferme de la Saugrenière, près de La Poitevinière. [...] Conduit à Angers, Stofflet est condamné à mort par une commission militaire et fusillé le lendemain, 25 février.

evidence.claim: Major-general, then commander in chief of the Catholic and Royal Army of Anjou
evidence.excerpt: Il est nommé major-général de l'armée royaliste et, en 1794, succède à Henri de La Rochejaquelein comme général en chef.

evidence.claim: Private in a Swiss regiment in royal service
evidence.excerpt: Longtemps simple soldat dans un régiment suisse en France

r.en: Leader of the Anjou insurgents; took Saint-Florent-le-Vieil
Major-general of the Catholic and Royal Army
Commander in chief of the army of Anjou
Peace of Saint-Florent-le-Vieil
Rose again; captured and shot at Angers
